WL-1373 gave `internal/designdoc` a CommonMark fence check (`openFence`, `closesFence` in `designdoc.go`). Four other scanners still treat any line starting with three backticks (some also `~~~`) as a fence toggle, so a line such as ```` ```` ```{mermaid} ```` text ```` flips them and everything after it is misread:

- `internal/gate/cite.go` `isFence`: the spec gate's citation check skips or scans the wrong lines.
- `internal/cmd/sharedinstructions.go` (around line 51)
- `internal/cmd/instructions.go` (around lines 163 and 242; backticks only)
- `internal/cli/ansimd.go` `openingFence`: terminal Markdown rendering.

Fix: move the two functions into a stdlib-only leaf package (for example `internal/mdfence`), have `internal/designdoc` call it, and switch the four scanners to it. A leaf package keeps `internal/cli`, which `lode-hook` imports, from pulling in `internal/designdoc` and its YAML dependency (`internal/disttest/deps_test.go` guards that closure).

- [ ] Each scanner has a test with a backtick line whose info string contains a backtick, and a four-backtick fence holding a three-backtick line.
- [ ] `internal/disttest` stays green.
